rv.q: Overall, David Copperfield is an imaginative piece of theatre that is truly well worth the watching but is even better if you brush up on your Dickens first.
Price and the cast have infused delightful stagecraft into this production.
Her direction is droll, very rarely buffoonish, and clips along with skill.
But Guildford’s Copperfield is dull as tarnished brass: the laughs are labored, the sparkle is incidental, and there is little indication of what puts the Dickens in Dickens.

The condensation of the masterpiece is skillfully done. From the sudden appearance at David’s birth of his man-hating great-aunt, Betsey Trotwood, the action hurtles forward. As Betsey awaits the delivery of a girl, she receives the periodic reports of the housekeeper Peggotty: “Peggotty?

cn.t: This three-actor adaptation delivers spirited performances and ingenious staging that keeps the narrative moving, though critics are divided on whether the compressed format captures the novel's depth and character development.
